explanation: Hamelin is a real town in Germany. When the town refused to pay him, the piper led its children away too, a story Robert Browning retold in an 1842 poem.

claims.text: In the legend, the Pied Piper of Hamelin lures the town's rats away with his pipe.
The Pied Piper does not lead locusts, wasps or snakes out of Hamelin.
Hamelin (Hameln) is a real town in Germany.
In the legend, when Hamelin refuses to pay the piper, he leads the town's children away.
Robert Browning published his poem The Pied Piper of Hamelin in 1842.
